findings.text: The mock persist helper re-derives the stage as `kwargs["score"] >= kwargs["min_score"] and not hold_records.open_holds()`, so the assertion at :167 compares the test's own copy of the acceptance rule against the test's own computation and would still pass if the product's hold-aware predicate were reverted. The acceptance logic is guarded for real against a disposable graph by tests/standard_names/test_review_holds.py.

_promote_if_eligible accepts on score-plus-no-open-hold alone, omitting the name_stage='accepted', quarantine exclusion and winning-review eligibility that PROMOTE_STRANDED_DOCS_WHERE applies, so dismissing the last hold on a quarantined or review-less docs_stage='reviewed' row accepts it outside the canonical gate.

The promote_stranded_reviewed row still documents acceptance on the stored score alone, so the repository operator reference contradicts the open-hold requirement the landed predicate adds to graph_ops.py:12557.
